subject: Can INLA be used to model 3D Cartesian data?

messages.author: 6329a3437b5a8591
messages.subject: Can INLA be used to model 3D Cartesian data?
parts:
Hi, all


I am wondering whether INLA can be applied to model y=f(x)+\epsilon, x \in R^3, \epsilon is Gaussian noise? 

In INLA, \alpha=2 by default, and 0=<\alpha<2 is also possible.  Since \alpha=\nu+d/2 and d=3 in our case, I am not sure whether \nu=1/2 can properly model the data correlation. 

On the other hand , does "2" in "inla.spde2.matern" in INLA means only x \in R^2 can be modeled, not for 3D data?


Looking forward to your reply!

Kindly Regards
Liye

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can INLA be used to model 3D Cartesian data?
parts:
It's possible, yes, but we don't have a simple interface for 3D spde domains yet.
For now, you'd have to construct the sparse finite element matrices for your 3D domain yourself, and call inla.spde2.generic() to construct the model object. How easy or hard that would be depends on your domain. I'm currently working on some updates for the mesh & spde models, so there may soon be some basic support for this built into the package.  What kind of domain and discretisation are you interested in?  A tetrahedralized domain, or a 3D lattice?

Finn
